current.text: Ja Morant was traded to Portland. Memphis got no draft capital for him.
Ty Jerome is expected to start at point guard.
Morant was the only real usage competition, so his exit opens a big role. Cameron Boozer is a main beneficiary.
Cameron Boozer will start and should do more as the season goes on.
The roster is very deep. Coach Tuomas Iisalo runs an 11-man rotation.
Joe expects only Cameron Boozer and Cedric Coward to play more than 30 minutes per game.
The guard group is crowded: Javon Small, Ty Jerome, Scotty Pippen Jr., Campazzo and Cam Spencer.
The frontcourt is crowded too: Prosper, Hendricks, Zach Edey and Isaiah Stewart all compete for minutes.
Memphis has too many players, mostly forwards, so more trades or cuts must happen.

Joe projects Ty Jerome, Cedric Coward, Jerami Grant, Cameron Boozer and Zach Edey as starters. The current depth chart starts Jaylen Wells instead of Grant and lists Grant on the second unit. The last starting forward spot is open.
In late June, Zach Edey was reported to have a broken foot.
Memphis tanked late last season. That is why Zach Edey was shut down.
Memphis will not be a good team.
Joe predicts wins in the low to mid 30s, around the 10th seed. He says Memphis is not trying to tank because of the new tanking rules.
Memphis has three first-round picks in the 2027 draft, so it has room to make trades. Jerami Grant is a possible trade piece.
Memphis has the fewest back-to-backs in the league, so its players carry less rest risk.
The fantasy playoff schedule is the best in the league: 4 games in each of weeks 19, 20 and 21.

durable.text: Coach Tuomas Iisalo plays at a very high pace.
Iisalo uses short stints of about five minutes and keeps player minutes down.
Memphis usually fills its roster with guaranteed contracts for flexibility and then waives players later.

note: Memphis plays very fast and has the best fantasy playoff schedule in the league, but Iisalo runs an 11-man rotation and keeps minutes short. That caps everyone except Cameron Boozer and Cedric Coward, who gain the most from Morant leaving. Early on, watch Zach Edey's foot, whether Grant or Wells starts at forward, and roster cuts or trades. Also check whether a weak team rests players late despite the new tanking rules.
